papers.name: Literature tracking
papers.description: Track new papers from the past week around the project's research focus, grouped by topic with findings, reading recommendations and source links.
papers.prompt:
Find relevant literature published or posted in the past seven days, using the current project's established research direction, keywords and topics without assuming a particular discipline. Prioritize scholarly indexes, journal websites and preprint platforms appropriate to the field. Deduplicate preprints and published versions and identify their publication status. If the project's research focus is unclear, state what information is missing rather than inventing a discipline or keywords.

Group results by topic and select 5–10 highly relevant papers worth reading. If fewer than five qualify, report the actual number without adding irrelevant papers. For each, include the original title, authors, journal or platform, publication date, DOI or source link, 1–2 sentences on the research question and key findings, and its relevance to the project and reason for recommendation. Use verifiable sources only. Clearly label abstract-only access and do not infer full-text conclusions.

Write the literature briefing in the current system language, retaining original paper titles. Start with 3–5 highlights and close with emerging trends and priority reads. State when no relevant new papers are found. Recommend papers only; do not automatically add them to the library.

report.name: Project report
report.description: Review this week's conversations and research outputs, summarize progress, findings and blockers, and propose next week's actions.
report.prompt:
Prepare a weekly report from the current project's accessible conversations, research outputs and new or updated materials from this week. Include only documented progress, distinguishing completed, ongoing and unconfirmed work. Do not assume undocumented work is complete.

Use the current system language and include: 1) 3–5 weekly highlights; 2) a progress table listing each research question or task, status, progress and supporting conversation or material; 3) key findings and recorded decisions, with evidence, limitations and conclusions awaiting validation; 4) blockers and information requiring user confirmation; 5) prioritized proposed actions for next week, with specific steps and expected outputs. Include owners and deadlines only when explicitly recorded; otherwise mark them as unconfirmed rather than making commitments.

Retain usable project source links or file paths, consolidate repeated discussions and avoid a chat transcript dump. Clearly state when there is no substantive progress or insufficient accessible material. Do not modify original materials or automatically create or assign tasks.

files.name: Organize materials
files.description: Inventory project materials and monthly changes, build a categorized index, and flag possible duplicates, unclear versions and missing information.
files.prompt:
Inventory the current project's accessible files, literature and research outputs, focusing on materials added or updated in the past month. Mark uncertain modification dates rather than treating all materials as new this month.

Write a report in the current system language containing: 1) 3–5 highlights about the collection and monthly changes; 2) a searchable index grouped by research topic and purpose, with each item's name, type, brief description, verified update time and original link or path; 3) possible duplicates, unclear version relationships, ambiguous names and unreadable materials, with the basis for each flag; 4) suggested missing materials and an organization order based on the project's established research goals.

Summarize only content actually read. For unread materials, list metadata and state access limitations. Mark unverifiable duplicate or version relationships as unconfirmed. If the project has no materials, say so and suggest how to begin organizing them. Produce an inventory and recommendations only; do not move, rename, overwrite or delete files, automatically merge literature records or change classifications.
